background: Deutsche Bank is Germany's largest bank, a universal bank with a large investment bank, a corporate bank, German retail banking under the Deutsche and Postbank brands, and the DWS asset manager.
synthesis: All three of the main agencies rate the bank, A+ on average and A at the weakest of them, two on a positive outlook and one on stable, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026 — an unusually large move and the clearest signal in the file. The ratios have not caught up with the ratings: CET1 of 13.9%, leverage of 4.5% and LCR of 140% are all in the bottom quarter of EU and Nordic banks and NSFR of 118% is below the peer median. None of the four has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026), so the position is stable rather than improving. Flagged items are numerous but of a familiar kind, litigation and settlements plus a client fraud that surfaced on 25 Sep 2026, and are better read as running conduct costs than as events in themselves.
